title: release-runway-sprint-prep-and-hotpatch-playbook
content:
Purpose: quick reference for the weekly release-runway sync (pre-sprint cut, canary metrics, hotpatch readiness). This is a working doc — notes, decisions, and action items for the release engineering + SRE handoff.

Attendees: Anika (RE lead), Rohit (infra), Lena (SRE), Connor (release eng), Maeve (prod-ops), guests: Tanya (serving-runtime), Victor (observability).

Meeting date: 2024-11-12 (captured ongoing updates through 2024-11-18)

Agenda (short):
- Quick status: active trains, capacity, and any embargoes
- Canary health window and metrics to validate
- Hotpatch queue: priority and owner assignment
- Rollforward / rollback playbook review and gaps
- Preflight checklist for next sprint release

Summary notes (raw):
- Active trains: Train-16 (feature) scheduled for 11/20 cut; Train-15 still in ramp with some tail latency spikes on NVMe-backed instances. We flagged one model quantization regression (PR link above).
- Capacity: Reserved pool at 78% utilization. Rohit: expecting an extra 4 gpus from Dedicated pool by 11/16 to support stress test. If delayed, fallback is to throttle batch sizes for non-critical routes (see batching knob plan below).
- Canary health: Lena ran the dry canary yesterday. Primary checks: p95 latency, token-throughput/sec, 5xx ratio. Current thresholds proposed: p95 < 220ms for short prompts (<256 tokens), 5xx < 0.5% sustained over 10 minutes, token throughput within 10% of baseline. Metrics dashboard: OBS/Canary-Runway (linked in Slack #release-runway).
- Observed anomaly: during last canary we saw KV cache hit-rate dip from 92% -> 76% when sequence lengths varied; possible cause: mishandled cache key normalization in the quantized path (Tanya to triage).

Decisions made:
- Canary gating: must pass both automated smoke + 30 minute steady-state window with none of the critical alerts firing. If p95 breaches twice within the window, auto-fail. (Owner: Lena)
- Hotpatch triage priority: security > customer-severity-1 > degradation. Hotpatch rollout to follow fast track: 1) patch build -> smoke -> canary -> global ramp. No manual skip to global without 3/4 signoffs. (Owner: Connor)
- Rollforward plan: if global rollout causes sustained 5xx >1% for 15 minutes or error budget burn >10% in 1h, trigger rollforward to previous compatible model variant. That rollback is orchestrated via router policy version pin (SRE-runbook step 4). (Owner: Rohit + Maeve)

Action items (with rough SLAs):
- Tanya: root cause triage for KV cache key normalization in quantized path; open a PR/branch for a deterministic key hashing fix. Target: 2024-11-14 EOD. Linked: serving-runtime PR template.
- Rohit: confirm extra 4 GPUs readiness and provide ETA; if delayed beyond 11/16 noon, provide temporary autoscale profile change. Target: 2024-11-15 AM.
- Lena: finalize canary dashboard panels and add automated chart annotations for gating events (p95/5xx/kvcache). Target: 2024-11-13.
- Connor: produce a short playback checklist for hotpatch fast-track (6-step checklist). Target: 2024-11-14.
- Maeve: update the runbook section on routing fallback to include example commands and a pre-approved list of engineers with permission to initiate rollforward. Target: 2024-11-18.

Hotpatch queue (snapshot):
- JIRA-HOTFIX-881: urgent dependency CVE bump in model-tokenizer: priority P0, owner: Connor, blocked by build failing on gcc-12.
- JIRA-HOTFIX-872: analytics emitter duplicate events causing SLO noise: P1, owner: Rohit.
- JIRA-HOTFIX-865: customer-facing snippet truncation bug on long prompts: P2, owner: Maeve.

Preflight checklist (for sprint release):
- Code: all PRs merged with green CI, release branch created, changelog compiled. (status: in progress)
- Infra: capacity validated for peak qps, autoscale test ran. (status: waiting on Rohit)
- Canary: dashboard ready, smoke script updated with new seed prompts, synthetic traffic generator tuned. (status: Lena todo)
- Observability: trace hooks verified, error budget alarms staged, log retention for release window increased to 30 days.
- Compliance: any private deployment customers notified if model variant changes affect on-prem packaging (product to confirm).

Mitigation playbook (short):
1) Detect (observability rule fires or canary failure) -> page on-call SRE (pager)
2) Assess (15 minute triage: gather logs, traces, key metrics)
3) Contain (pin routing to standby variant; reduce batch size on high-latency routes)
4) Patch or rollback (hotpatch path or router pin rollback)
5) Postmortem (owner opens postmortem ticket within 48 hours)

Notes on automation and knobs: (informal brainstorming)
- Consider a small autoscale-window buffer for canaries to avoid spurious p95 blips from scheduling jitter.
- Add a preflight synthetic workload that includes sequence-length variance to exercise KV cache heat; this reduces false negatives in canaries.
- Introduce a small 'quiet window' during global ramp where non-critical background jobs are deprioritized (reduce background batching).

Risks and unresolved questions: (short bullets)
- Our canary synthetic suite doesn't reflect some real-customer prompt patterns (long-tail sequences). Need input from product on sample prompts. (Action: Maeve)
- Are the on-call permissions for rollforward sufficiently audited? We should list 3 backups. (Action: Anika)
- Quantization path regression frequency unknown across model catalog; we need sweep across top 10 served models. (Action: Tanya + Research)

Next sync: Tuesday 2024-11-19 10:30 PT (pre-sprint cut). We'll run a 20-minute focused sync on canary readiness and hotpatch blockers. If critical blockers are resolved earlier, we'll close this doc and push owners to their respective JIRA tickets.

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts (scratch):
- Keep this doc lean; move longplaybook to Confluence after we stabilize the checklist.
- Add example rollback router CLI snippet in runbook: `redwood router pin --route my-route --model my-model:vN` (ops note).

Attachments / references: add to confluence: Release Runway Playbook draft, link code PRs and the canary dashboard snapshots.

End of meeting notes.
